pages.reason: A novice needs time to trace the two-document mask in the diagram and the printed four rows, then distinguish isolated packing from merely causal attention. The position-reset, cross-boundary targets, and GPU quality/timing comparisons add brief reasoning beyond the small mask program.

The main pause is checking why losses from one and two samples must share a denominator of three: the printed gradients 9.3333, 9.3333 and 7.5 make unequal weighting concrete. Effective-token counts, update order, and the training memory/time comparison require further careful reading.

This page combines floating-point range versus precision, a BF16 matrix product, and loss scaling. Reading the actual 0.0075 difference is quick; understanding successful versus skipped updates, two experimental tables, answer quality, and unequal memory baselines takes several additional pauses.

Tracing Q/K/V axes, the causal diagram, scaling, and the True-as-allowed mask takes deliberate attention before interpreting the CPU shape and 5.96e-08 difference. The whole-model comparison and separate forced-Flash probe add backend, gradient, and tolerance distinctions a novice must keep straight.

The reader must work through changing the softmax maximum and rescaling both accumulated numerator and denominator, matching the diagram to the printed 1.5/25 and 1.75/42.5. The second figure and four-row cost table require distinguishing incremental allocation from the common 65 MiB baseline.

The code needs a pause to separate independent input gradients from the shared layer gradients accumulated by two backward calls; both printed differences are zero. The reader then connects recomputation to saved activations, random-state consistency, and the actual time-versus-memory tradeoff.

The arithmetic break-even examples are accessible, but the reader must distinguish eager-backend interface agreement from true compilation. The printed hypothetical totals, delayed first-call work, and the Inductor result with no speed saving need brief comparison and interpretation.

The independent introduction only asks the reader to connect fewer storage bits with lost numerical detail and follow the chapter's progression from scales to packing and answer checks. It contains no teaching code, CPU output, or figure to study.

The simple dtype output is easy to follow, but the full-model byte table needs careful addition of quantized coefficients, retained FP32 values, bias, and scales. Distinguishing tensor payload, file metadata, optimizer state, and runtime memory adds conceptual work beyond multiplying 2048 elements.

The diagram and four-value CPU output support tracing divide, round, clamp, and restore. A novice still needs to think about lost offsets, half-grid error, unused -128, ties-to-even, and why the displayed decimal tails differ from formatted four-place text.

The reader should hand-check at least one dot product and see why the same 0.2 weight errors either add or cancel, matching the actual output-difference matrix. Matrix orientation, MAE, floating display tails, input scaling, and later nonlinear effects make this more than a quick formula read.

Following -1,0,1,2 through codes 0,5,10,15 gives a compact zero-point example, but understanding why code zero differs from floating zero requires a pause. The min/max expansion to include zero, fifteen intervals, and uint8 versus packed four-bit storage also need attention.

The two printed integer matrices make the small row disappearing under a global scale easy to see. The reader needs extra thought to connect per-channel with output rows, compare the two row-MAE values, and balance improved precision against more scales and grouping metadata.

This comparison asks the reader to interpret average and maximum error together, then distinguish seventeen ideal four-bit bytes from the actual thirty-three-byte int8 container. The ceiling-byte arithmetic and values that fit a coarse grid exactly deserve a short manual check.

The fixed two-row layer is manageable, but the printed uint8 storage and float32 output require separating packed representation from floating computation. Checking the ten-byte total, the 0.5143 result, buffer roles, and retained full-model modules adds a few pauses.

The binary diagram needs deliberate tracing because the first value enters the low nibble while the second enters the high nibble. Matching 112,152,175,139 to the seven original integers, the pad code, shifts and masks is the main thinking work; full-model scale/bias accounting follows.

The reader follows a deep-copied model through conversion and checks the unchanged original against the printed zero difference and 0.0290 score MAE. The trained-source update history, untouched embeddings, shared-weight caveat, and activation-PTQ distinction require careful attribution rather than just reading the helper call.

The printed 8320,1280,1024 byte figures are useful anchors for separating the whole layer from codes alone. A novice needs further time to understand temporary dequantized weights, specialized kernels, the timing comparison, and allocated/reserved/driver memory before judging what storage reduction means.

The reader compares three small output matrices and the actual MAEs 0.19 and 0.24, pausing over the off-diagonal errors that cancel when inputs are also quantized. Fixed-scale simulation, changing activation ranges, and the absence of activation quantization in the reported GPU experiments need clear separation.

The fixed-versus-dynamic CPU results show a straightforward but important tradeoff: clipping 3 to 1 versus losing -0.2 to zero. The reader then needs time for calibration versus independent evaluation, percentile ranges, runtime work, and why adding an evaluation value to calibration is only a controlled example.

The main pause is reconciling much better small-value MAE with an extreme-value error of 99 and worse total MAE. Reading the actual clipped and unclipped vectors supports this, while separate validation and test roles prevent interpreting the most attractive metric as a universal win.

Understanding how detach yields rounded forward values yet STE gradients of one requires a deliberate derivation alongside the three-stage diagram. The six experimental branches, matched 350-update packed comparison, reversed validation/test ordering, deployment-format check, and displayed workflow commands add substantial reading and interpretation.

The short CPU example proves that a 0.005 MAE can switch the choice from cat to EOS; the reader should pause over that boundary. The rest requires connecting numerical differences to actual token IDs, answer quality, formatting/behavior checks, matched experiment sources, and generation settings.

The preface introduces teacher signals, a genuinely smaller student, alignment, and cost while warning that connected mechanisms can still fail. A short pause to understand the preserved attribute, style, and story failures is sufficient; generated navigation contributes no extra time.

The two actual CPU lines both choose 4 but retain different distributions, so the reader must think about what information a text answer discards. Black-box versus white-box access, teacher provenance and poor held-out ability, tokenization, and distribution-storage cost add conceptual reading.

The printed teacher and student counts make structural shrinkage concrete. The reader needs a pause to see why width and depth reductions do not scale every parameter equally, then distinguish architecture size from the learning signal in matched CE, hard-target, and KL branches.

The JSON filtering example is approachable, but the reader must distinguish its artificial source from actual teacher-generated targets. The date errors, original-ID/EOS auditing, no-empty-target rules, retokenization, and teacher-generation/verification costs require careful reading beyond the single accepted record.

A novice needs to check the weighted negative-log arithmetic and interpret the actual score-gradient signs, especially why the already-matched candidate gets zero soft-target gradient. Reading hard versus soft targets and the wrong-teacher variant adds thinking that the two CE numbers alone do not convey.

The probability-ratio derivation and three-color temperature figure invite manual comparison with the three CPU distributions. Additional pauses are needed to separate unchanged ranking from increased secondary mass, understand the once-only T-squared convention, and keep distillation temperature distinct from generation sampling.

Tracing the crossed cat/dog lines and the printed reorder [1,0] is simple, but it takes thought to connect numeric shape equality with semantic misalignment. Token granularity, identical prediction contexts, special tokens, and the real effective-label cache alignment broaden the lesson beyond a permutation.

The four CPU observations require distinguishing eval, frozen weights, no_grad and optimizer membership: the teacher stays unchanged while differentiable inputs still build a graph. The actual cache and hard-answer costs then need interpretation as reusable but nonzero work.

The reader must check directed KL, including its negative individual term, and connect the label mask to the zero first-row gradient and two half-sized contributions in the CPU output. The kl_div argument order, teacher forcing, T², and CE-minus-entropy derivation add several meaningful mathematical pauses.

The printed 0.6931,0.4429,0.1927 losses support a short interpolation check, but the reader must compare which truth and teacher preferences each term represents. The conflicting second position, alpha-zero assertion, and once-only T² convention need thought before interpreting a smaller mixed loss.

The constructed 10-versus-50-second records are easy, but the actual matched-width student table needs comparison of NLL, exact answers, teacher agreement, and token budgets. The two complete out-of-domain questions and 198 excluded inputs also require careful interpretation of the narrow benchmark scope.

The CPU agreement of one versus acceptance of only one-third prompts a useful pause about task truth and alternative uncertainty wording. The larger style experiment then separates valid JSON, EOS, date matching, arithmetic failures, and lower teacher-forced NLL from successful generated content.

Reading the common 264-candidate shapes is quick, but the reader must understand why different hidden widths and experts can still support KL. The actual story-data budget, fragments and one EOS per story, NLL improvement, and repeated generated phrases demand a slower comparison of what was and was not preserved.

This page needs the most alignment thought: the reader traces the one-position prediction shift through the diagram and printed 15–17 versus 3–5 rows, then through two real examples. Changed patch sizes, four matched student runs, quality tables, paired blank-input behavior, and workflow commands add substantial interpretation.

The printed payloads require distinguishing fewer parameters from fewer bits and remembering buffers. The four-stage real table and the blue-to-ble failure then need a pause to attribute quality changes to distillation or later quantization; the story comparison and storage/runtime limits extend that judgment.

The two-paragraph preface asks the reader to connect separately working components with a complete assistant and understand the limits of its small world. It introduces the staged route and distinguishes short mechanism examples from full training; there is no code, output or figure in this own preface.

The reader studies three action types and the actual parser output, then compares eight real successes and failures across media and tools. Understanding action versus end-to-end correctness and the displayed JSON/CLI/web trial workflow takes time, while installation, downloading and running the trial are excluded.

The workshop figure and CPU counts require separating all stored experts from the active structural proxy. The same-width Dense contrast, nearer-active random Dense benchmark, and memory/time scope add careful comparison; the reader must resist equating active counts with speed, quality, or complete memory use.

The nested dictionaries, set intersections and Counters take a novice time to trace against the detailed CPU task totals. More thought is needed for family versus actual-input leakage, held-out combinations, balanced audio, constant image baselines, and why zero overlap still does not prove generalization.

The reader follows the four-stage diagram and parent-checkpoint chain, then connects the printed 43 versus 10 targets to different learning objectives. The training table, per-modality validation counts, auxiliary/CE budgets, and full SHA comparison require deliberate attribution of continuity versus ability.

The four concrete CPU demonstrations make the desired behavior readable, but the reader must distinguish data examples from generated success. The validation examples, fixed-template and constant-answer limitations, raw-ID-to-question lookup, and preservation across joint/DPO stages require additional interpretation.

The tensor/label CPU check is only the starting point. The reader must track two uses of joint, different pitch conventions, summary-feature losses, stage-wise validation, and paired image/audio changes; especially the unchanged circle answer that becomes correct only after swapping shape. Several tables and concrete failures merit sustained thought.

The tool-loop diagram and CPU runtime success/error are straightforward, but the reader must keep the manual request separate from model-generated requests and final answers. Parameter-order rules, separate denominators, and the actual 0+1 and 1+0 readback failures require careful step-by-step interpretation.

The DPO example needs time to identify same-fact chosen/rejected answers and the fixed reference behind the printed 0.6931 loss. The mixed training objective, different-batch loss comparison, lost multimodal answers, validation-based selection, and the student's different teacher lineage require several attribution pauses.

The reader traces the three-position cache plus two new positions and the CPU 5.36e-07 agreement before comparing the same final token. The twelve-task multimodal consistency probe and separate one-prompt timing table add important distinctions in generation IDs, stopping limits and measured scope.

The small CPU layer introduces payload and approximation, but the two deployment tables require tracking source joint, DPO teacher, CE student and KD student separately. Equal scores with changed IDs, wrong tool parameters and readback, and retained FP32 computation add substantial quality-versus-storage reasoning.

The actual temporary save/load output is short, but understanding what it proves requires separating architecture metadata from training history. The eleven public formats, pinned checksums, inference commands, four-stage training commands and resume contracts need careful reading; downloading, execution and training waits are excluded.
